search_intent: A Mercer Island homeowner planning a sunroom wants to know whether the City requires a permit, whether it is a small or substantial addition, how lot coverage, gross floor area and setbacks limit it, how geohazard, wet season and shoreline rules apply, what the Washington energy code says about sunroom glass and sloped glazing, and how to hire a registered contractor.
local_angles: Mercer Island small additions: under 500 sf new footprint and impervious surface, no critical area
Lot coverage tied to lot slope (40/35/30/20%) and GFA capped at 40% of net lot area
Geohazard work is very common on Mercer Island; geotech report by WA-licensed engineer
No clearing, grading, filling or foundation work Oct 1-Apr 1 on slope hazard lots without waiver
Shoreline permitting within 200 ft of Lake Washington OHWM
2021 WSEC-R: sunroom glazing under 60 degrees counts as skylight
Inspections on MyBuildingPermit.com; City Hall currently closed
